## Best power station for RV boondocking under $1,000 (2026)

**My top pick is the BLUETTI AC200L**, particularly if you want to power an RV through a 30A connection rather than just charge individual devices.

  <AsyncImage query="BLUETTI AC200L portable power station product white background" aspectRatio="4:5" maxWidth="160px"/>
  <box flex="1" gap={1}>
    <title size="lg">BLUETTI AC200L</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">Best for RV integration</text>
    <title size="xl" color="default">$899</title>
    <text color="secondary" size="xs">2,048Wh LiFePO4 · 2,400W output · 30A RV outlet</text>
    <text size="sm">A strong combination of battery capacity, appliance power, and RV connectivity.</text>
    <text size="sm"><Link url="https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv" title="RV comparison and pricing"/></text>
  </box>
</row>

The supplied search results also describe a promotional price of **$854.05** with code `AFF5OFF`, although I haven't independently verified that the discount still applies.

## How it compares

| Power station | Capacity | Output | Listed price |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **BLUETTI AC200L** | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $899 |
| Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 | 2,042Wh | 2,200W | $999 |
| Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 | 1,024Wh | 2,000W | $699 |
| EcoFlow DELTA 2 Max | 2,048Wh | 2,400W | $999 |

These are prices reported by the supplied 2026 search results, not live checkout prices.

## Why I'd choose the BLUETTI

- **2kWh battery:** More practical for overnight fridge, lighting, and electronics use than a 1kWh unit.
- **2,400W inverter:** Can handle many common RV appliances, subject to startup surge requirements.
- **30A RV connection:** Convenient for compatible RV setups, though it does not provide the full 3,600W of a conventional 120V/30A shore-power hookup.
- **LiFePO4 chemistry:** Well suited to repeated charging and discharging.

The main drawback is that the AC200L is an older model, with one source reporting it discontinued in Canada.

For lighter weekend camping, I'd choose the **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 at $699** instead. For extended boondocking, the additional capacity of the BLUETTI is worth prioritizing.

**Bottom line:** Buy the BLUETTI AC200L if you can confirm the sub-$900 price, warranty, and availability. Budget separately for solar panels if you need to stay off-grid for multiple days. A 2kWh station is not enough for sustained RV air-conditioning use.

Sources: <Link url="https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv" title="Dealectric RV comparison"/>, <Link url="https://volt-vanguard.com/article/portable-power-station-for-rv/" title="VoltVanguard 2026 RV guide"/>, and <Link url="https://sunenergytechnology.com/blog/best-portable-power-station-under-1000.html" title="2026 budget comparison"/>.
